text.name: ml_helpQsMapSlots

text.name: ml_uiIntro
text.text: Redefine the layers? Current: %s. The editor asks for each overburden layer's material and lower boundary in metres, then for the pay seam below them (PAYDIRT by default, coal or limestone work too). The bedrock at the very bottom stays fixed - that is where digging ends.

text.name: ml_edSummarySection
text.text: Resulting profile

text.name: ml_edScope
text.text: You are editing the standard: it applies to every area without its own layers, including the ones already drawn. To give a single pit its own layers, simply pick that area under Applies to above.

text.name: ml_edScopeGlobal
text.text: You are editing the layers for “Everywhere”: they apply across the whole map, with no area to draw. An area you have assigned to a machine takes priority — and where an area has a material entered, normal TerraFarm applies.

text.name: ml_helpManEditor4
text.text: Standard and exceptions: what you save with All areas is the standard — it applies to every area without its own layers, retroactively to the existing ones too. If a single pit should differ, pick it under Applies to above and save its layers — right in the editor, no file editing needed.

text.name: ml_edScopeArea

text.name: ml_edActiveOff

text.name: ml_helpQsBothWaysTitle
text.text: Two ways — you decide per area

text.name: ml_helpQsBothWays1
text.text: Leave the material fields on the TerraFarm area EMPTY and Mining Layers does its job: what ends up in the bucket depends on how deep you dig. That is the normal case for a pit.

text.name: ml_helpQsBothWays2
text.text: Enter a material on the area instead and you get plain TerraFarm without layers. Exactly right for construction sites, road building and levelling — anywhere you just want to move soil and always need the same material.

text.name: ml_helpQsBothWays3
text.text: You get the same result from the Layers tab: pick an area there and set it to "Plain TerraFarm". Both routes lead to the same place, take whichever you prefer.

text.name: ml_edForeign
text.text: ⚠ This zone was hand-written in miningLayers.xml and can only be shown here in simplified form. Saving rewrites it in the editor’s own scheme; a fixed reference height is lost. Custom ground textures (paintLayer) are kept.

text.name: ml_edAdd
text.text: Add layer

text.name: ml_edRemove
text.text: Remove layer

text.name: ml_edSaved
text.text: Layers saved. They apply right away to every area without its own zone.

text.name: ml_edHint
text.text: The bright outline marks the layer you are editing. The pay seam is the fixed last row: material selectable (PAYDIRT by default, coal or limestone work too), thickness and position fixed. The rock below goes in on its own. Minimum thickness: 1 m for the top layer, 1.5 m for every layer below — with big machines better go 2 m. Do not forget to save: ESC or Back leaves the page and everything since your last save is discarded.

text.name: ml_edPoolMissing

text.name: ml_edPoolHint
text.text: Rule of thumb: fewer mods = more free slots = more materials you can dump.

text.name: ml_helpQsSetupTitle
text.text: Set up in one step

text.name: ml_helpQsSetup1
text.text: Draw a TerraFarm area around your pit and leave the fields inside it empty. That is the whole setup. Dig anywhere in that area and the material comes from the depth instead of the vehicle setting. Important: assign the area to your machine as its INPUT AREA (machine menu, default Y) - TerraFarm links areas to the machine, not to your position.

text.name: ml_helpQsSetup2
text.text: The mod works out the reference height itself: it reads the terrain heights at the corner points of your area and derives the surface from them. Nothing to read off, nothing to type in. If you do enter a material on the area, you get plain TerraFarm without layers. Handy for construction work.

text.name: ml_helpQsStockNote
text.text: Every image here shows the mod as it ships: topsoil, gravel, paydirt, rock, with nobody having set up a single layer by hand. That is what you get once the area is drawn. Your own layers are an option, not a requirement.

text.name: ml_helpQsDisplayTitle
text.text: The readout on the left

text.name: ml_helpQsDisplay1
text.text: While a machine is active, the left of the screen tells you where you are: current height, which layer you are working and how many metres are left until the next one.

text.name: ml_helpQsDisplayB1
text.text: That readout is what counts, not TerraFarm's material field. The vehicle keeps showing its own setting and is only overridden at the moment you dig.

text.name: ml_helpQsDisplayB2
text.text: Move it in game: Num * (rebindable) toggles the move mode with a mouse cursor - pick up, drop, done. Switch it off with Num / or showHeightDisplay in miningLayers.xml.

text.name: ml_helpQsLayersTitle
text.text: Setting your own layers

text.name: ml_helpQsLayers1
text.text: Out of the box: topsoil, gravel below it, then paydirt, rock at the bottom. That fits almost any pit, so there is nothing you have to set up.

text.name: ml_helpQsWizardButton
text.text: Set up layers

text.name: ml_helpQsWizardHint
text.text: You do not have to, though. Do nothing and our default applies, which fits almost any pit. Want it different? Go to the Layers tab, build your own profile there and watch it take shape as you go.

text.name: ml_helpQsLayersScope
text.text: You edit the overburden layers and the pay seam below them (PAYDIRT by default, coal or limestone work too). Its position stays fixed: whoever wants the ore has to dig through the overburden — real mining gameplay instead of material at the push of a button. The rock at the very bottom is placed by the mod itself.

text.name: ml_helpQsMistakesTitle
text.text: The three mistakes when drawing an area

text.name: ml_helpQsWarnWater
text.text: Lake or shore: corner points in the water measure the bottom. The reference plane tilts and you hit rock at the shoreline. Keep the area mostly on land.

text.name: ml_helpQsWarnRidge
text.text: Mountain ridge: an area drawn across the ridge turns the reference plane into a chord and pushes paydirt near the surface. On a remote steep face that is the intended mountain bonus, on the hill behind your farm it is not. Draw slope areas on ONE face.

text.name: ml_helpQsRidgeCaption
text.text: On a steep face it reads like this: layer GRAVEL at 15.7 m, only 2.3 m left to the paydirt. Make the trip up the mountain and you get there sooner. That one is on purpose.

text.name: ml_helpQsWarnRiver
text.text: River crossing: with corners on both banks the riverbed in the middle sits far below the reference plane and the pit floor ends up under the bed, so the pit floods. Draw areas along the river, never across it.

text.name: ml_helpManWhatTitle
text.text: What the mod changes

text.name: ml_helpManWhat1
text.text: In FS25 you set on the vehicle what your bucket picks up, no matter how deep you dig. This mod gives the ground layers instead: what you get depends on how far below the surface your digging point sits.

text.name: ml_helpManWhat2
text.text: This is a pure runtime addon on top of TerraFarm. No TerraFarm file is modified and no third-party code is shipped. Without TerraFarm the mod stays silent.

text.name: ml_helpManLayersTitle
text.text: The layers

text.name: ml_helpManLayers1
text.text: Default from top to bottom: DIRT, then GRAVEL, then PAYDIRT, then STONE. Rock is the end of the line. That is deliberate, not a missing feature.

text.name: ml_helpManLayersB1
text.text: Depths are lower boundaries in metres below the surface, not absolute heights above sea level.

text.name: ml_helpManLayersB2
text.text: The bottom layer needs no boundary, it continues downwards without end.

text.name: ml_helpManLayersB3
text.text: Every layer gets a matching ground texture so you can see where you are in the hole. Use paintLayer to set it yourself per layer.

text.name: ml_helpManLayers2
text.text: Layers apply per area. An area without its own zone inherits the default layers, an area with a material entered gets none at all.

text.name: ml_helpManMoundTitle
text.text: Spoil heaps and backfilling

text.name: ml_helpManMound1
text.text: The mod remembers what you dumped where. Pick a heap back up and you get exactly what is in it, not the geology underneath. That holds anywhere on the map until the heap is gone.

text.name: ml_helpManMoundB1
text.text: Backfill your hole and you take the fill out again first. Only below that do the layers apply again.

text.name: ml_helpManMoundB2
text.text: Dig below the base of a heap and the heap is through at that spot, so geology returns. This stops you from shovelling endless material out of a crater.

text.name: ml_helpManMoundB3
text.text: Empty the bucket before changing layers. A container holds one material type only, and with the old load still in it the bucket will not take the new material.

text.name: ml_helpManEditorTitle
text.text: Setting your own layers

text.name: ml_helpManEditor1
text.text: The Layers tab is where you build your own profile. The cross-section is on the left, layer, material and thickness on the right. Six overburden layers at most; available are DIRT, SOIL, GRAVEL, SAND, STONE, COAL and LIMESTONE. Minimum thickness: 1 m for the top layer, 1.5 m for every layer below it — thinner layers break spoil pile pickup. With big machines, 2 m is the better choice.

text.name: ml_helpManEditor3
text.text: Leave the page with ESC or the Back button. Careful: changed is not saved. Only the Save button writes the layers and applies them right away to the target picked above — the standard or the single area. Leave before that and the old state is back next time you open it.

text.name: ml_helpManEditor2
text.text: You cannot pick PAYDIRT as overburden - the money material always sits BELOW the overburden. As the pay seam (last row in the editor) you can pick COAL, LIMESTONE, STONE, GRAVEL, SAND, DIRT or SOIL besides PAYDIRT: for gravel pits and coal country. The bedrock below stays fixed.

text.name: ml_helpManFloorTitle
text.text: The pit floor

text.name: ml_helpManFloor1
text.text: As long as you do not touch an area's target height yourself, the mod sets it below your deepest layer automatically - otherwise the pit ends where the editor put it while you were drawing: at ground level. Enlarge the area and the floor follows.

text.name: ml_helpManFloor2
text.text: Set the target height yourself (type it in, or use up/down in the area editor) and it is yours from then on: the mod never touches it again. That is how you level a pad, a berm or a ramp. The display tells you which one applies - "set by you" or "automatic".

text.name: ml_helpManConfigTitle
text.text: Configuring by hand

text.name: ml_helpManConfig1
text.text: Everything lives in modSettings/FS25_MiningLayers/miningLayers.xml. The file is created on first start and survives mod updates. Before the wizard saves for the first time, the mod puts a .bak next to it once per session.

text.name: ml_helpManConfig2
text.text: That is also where you toggle the readout, the depth lines, the automatic pit floor and the ground texture when dumping. Zones can be switched off individually or given their own layers per area.

text.name: ml_helpTipsTfTitle
text.text: TerraFarm pitfalls

text.name: ml_helpTipsTfB1
text.text: Turn defaultEnabled off, otherwise every TerraFarm vehicle churns up your yard just by driving.

text.name: ml_helpTipsTfB2
text.text: Lowering only works inside the polygon when Restrict area is set. Levelling works outside too. If nothing happens you are usually on the wrong side of the line. Or the ground is already at target height.

text.name: ml_helpTipsTfB3
text.text: A wheel loader only manages some 30 to 40 centimetres per pass. Build a ramp. The tool for depth is the excavator.

text.name: ml_helpTipsTfB4
text.text: The keys sit on the numpad, Num 9 opens the global settings. After changing them a clean exit and restart may be needed before they take effect.

text.name: ml_helpTipsTfB6
text.text: A dozer gets through the layers too: lower the blade, mode Flatten, and make the run long enough - the longer the pass, the deeper you get each time. The picture shows the second layer (gravel) reached with the blade alone - no rear ripper at all. At the boundary: use up old mounds first and empty the blade, until then the old material stays in it.

text.name: ml_helpTipsTfB5
text.text: Without an area, lowering has no lower limit, because the target height is sea level. The hole still only gets as deep as you dig it, but an area gives you a defined floor.

text.name: ml_helpTipsVehTitle
text.text: When a vehicle will not dig

text.name: ml_helpTipsVeh1
text.text: For a vehicle to dig at all, TerraFarm needs a machine configuration for it. Without one nothing happens, and that is down to neither TerraFarm nor this mod.

text.name: ml_helpTipsVehB1
text.text: Install a machines configuration, for example the official FS25_TerraFarmMachines by scfmod.

text.name: ml_helpTipsVehB2
text.text: Many mining vehicle packs ship their own machine entries. Duplicate entries do not make it better, they make it worse. Pick one.

text.name: ml_helpTipsVehB3
text.text: If a bucket shows the arrows but removes nothing, it is that bucket. Try another one on the same excavator: if that works, the tool's entry is at fault, not your setup.

text.name: ml_helpTipsVeh2
text.text: A configuration pack for the common mining machines is in the works. It will be released separately from this mod.

text.name: ml_helpTipsMapTitle
text.text: Map specifics

text.name: ml_helpTipsMapB1
text.text: How many ground materials are possible is set by the map, not by the mod — many allow 63, wider ones more, and the base game already uses 48. With many mods the rest goes fast and the last ones can no longer be dumped. The mod checks this at startup and writes the affected materials to the log.

text.name: ml_helpTipsMapB2
text.text: Ground texture names differ on every map. On your first dig the mod writes your map's list to the log. Take the paintLayer values from there.

text.name: ml_helpTipsMapB4
text.text: The mod runs on any map: for layer textures it automatically picks the closest ground the map offers (standard names like GRAVEL, MOUNTAINROCK, MOSS_STONES). If a map has nothing suitable, your own texture selection simply stays active - materials, layers and mounds still work.

text.name: ml_helpTipsMapB3
text.text: Some maps lock riverbeds against deformation. That is the map's own block map and has nothing to do with ownership or with this mod.

text.name: ml_helpTipsAboutTitle
text.text: About this mod

text.name: ml_helpTipsAbout1
text.text: Mining Layers is an unofficial addon for TerraFarm by scfmod. There is no affiliation with scfmod and no TerraFarm files are shipped. TerraFarm is available on GitHub, not on ModHub.

text.name: ml_pageTitle
text.text: Mining Layers

text.name: ml_credits
text.text: Mining Layers by Tommy Honold. A FrittePlayz project.

text.name: ml_helpQsMapTitle
text.text: First: which materials does YOUR map have?

text.name: ml_helpQsMap1
text.text: Whether a material exists at all, and whether you can dump it back onto the ground, is not decided by this mod but by your map together with your mod list. Of the mining materials the base game only knows STONE — DIRT, GRAVEL, SAND, COAL, LIMESTONE or PAYDIRT always come from maps or mods. On top of that every map has a limited number of ground slots: the base game already uses 48 of them, and how many exist in total is set by the map itself — many have 63, wider ones have more. Once a map has run out, you can still dig, haul and sell a material, but no longer dump it.

text.name: ml_helpQsMap2
text.text: Mining Layers therefore takes a middle road so it stays playable on every map: on map load it checks once what YOUR map actually provides and offers only that in the layer picker. A (!) behind a name means: digging, hauling and selling work, dumping does not on this map. Anything missing entirely is named under the cross-section. So you never have to test a map first or look anything up — if something is missing, it is the map, not the mod.

text.name: ml_helpQsMap3
text.text: Two ways out if a material you need carries a (!): drop mods that bring their own ground materials, or play a map that was built with more channels. The 63 are not a fixed law of the game — a map can be built wider, and some already are. What no mod can do is raise it from the outside.

text.name: ml_mapSection
text.text: What this map can do

text.name: ml_mapNoData
text.text: The map report is available once the map has loaded.

text.name: ml_mapUsable
text.text: Usable on this map: %s — you can dig, haul, sell and dump these back onto the ground.

text.name: ml_mapNoTipList
text.text: Dig and sell only: %s. Dumping back onto the ground does not work here — no ground slot left in the terrain system.

text.name: ml_mapMissingList
text.text: Not present at all: %s. Neither the map nor your mods provide these.

text.name: ml_mapAdvice
text.text: How many ground materials fit is decided by your MAP: it sets the channel width, and the base game already uses 48 slots. How many are used up is decided by your MOD LIST — first to load gets a slot. So: fewer mods frees slots, and a map built with more channels has more of them to begin with.

text.name: ml_mapManyOwn
text.text: This map brings a large number of ground materials of its own, so the slots run out early. That is typical for maps carried over from FS19 or FS22.

text.name: ml_helpTipsAbout2
text.text: This mod is free so far.
